newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bond broker tightens up on accounts practice.
newsitem.headline: Japan bond broker tightens up on accounts practice.

text.p: Japan Bond Trading Co Ltd, the nation's largest inter-dealer broker, said on Thursday it will extend its trading hours until 5 p.m. from next April by abolishing the practice of allowing bond trades done after 3.40 p.m. to be treated as the following day's transactions.
The practice has been criticised as allowing participants to manipulate profits and losses on their books.

This was expected to become especially troublesome after financial institutions adopt the market price method of accounting for their trading accounts from fiscal 1997/98, starting on April 1. The cost method, now in use, does not show unrealised profits or losses.
Eliminating the possibility of such manipulation is the chief aim of ending the practice, a company official said.
"Our clients agreed that the current practice is creating problems and therefore should be abolished," he said.
